record_identity.title: Persistent adversarial context or memory poisoning

summary: Attacker-controlled or untrusted state survives the originating content or interaction and remains retrievable or behaviourally operative in later inference, planning or execution without adequate provenance, quarantine, revocation or derivative-use suppression.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Persistent memory changes the security lifetime of hostile input. Ending the originating interaction, changing a password or removing the source does not necessarily remove the behaviour-shaping state.

failure_mode_definition: A failure in which adversarial or untrusted state persists beyond the originating content or interaction, remains capable of later retrieval or behavioural influence, and is accepted without adequate source provenance, quarantine, revocation, invalidation or derivative-use suppression.
failure_threshold: The threshold requires: persistence beyond the originating content or interaction; later reactivation, retrieval or behavioural effect; inadequate provenance, quarantine, revocation or invalidation; and a security-relevant consequence or credible pathway. Ordinary prompt injection confined to one interaction, training-data poisoning, general context contamination and cross-user memory leakage are excluded.

failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects demonstrated persistent attacker-controlled memory capable of later behavioural effect and connected-service data exposure, with the public evidence arising from controlled research rather than confirmed widespread exploitation.
failure_classification.likelihood: demonstrated in controlled security research; recurrence depends on deployment architecture and control coverage
failure_classification.confidence: high for the demonstrated mechanism; bounded for undisclosed provider internals and ecosystem prevalence
failure_classification.failure_scope: persistent memory, retrieval, summary and context stores
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur wherever untrusted content can write durable state that later influences higher-authority behaviour.
failure_classification.taxonomy_reference: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 §3.5.10 — Persistent Adversarial Context or Memory Poisoning; primary classification OPS.FF.SECURITY_INTEGRITY
failure_classification.persistence: Definitional: the state survives the originating content and remains operative until quarantined, revoked, invalidated or overwritten.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Testable through authorised attempts to write hostile state, remove the originating content, begin a later interaction and observe retrieval or behavioural effect.
failure_classification.visibility: Often latent until later retrieval or action; may survive ordinary credential or session changes.
